articles.summary: A digital upload portal improves document transmission but does not eliminate verification work. For high-volume evidence types, structured verifiable evidence can reduce manual interpretation while improving provenance.
articles.title: From PDF Uploads to Verifiable Evidence: Modernizing Benefits Documentation

articles.summary: FinCEN and four federal banking regulators have jointly confirmed that government-issued verifiable digital credentials, including mobile driver's licenses, qualify as documentary identification under the CIP Rule.
articles.title: FinCEN Confirms Banks Can Accept Digital Credentials. Now They Need to Verify Them.

articles.summary: Government services assume the person interacting is the person acting. AI agents challenge that assumption, creating new questions about authorization, identity proofing, and auditability.
articles.title: When an AI Agent Acts on Behalf of a Resident

articles.summary: Knowing who an agent represents is not enough. Enterprises need to know what that agent is allowed to do, with authority that is granular, portable, and revocable.
articles.title: AI Agents Have an Authorization Problem, Not Just an Identity Problem

articles.summary: Utah's SB 275 creates a legal framework for state-endorsed digital identity with 11 enumerated rights, a Duty of Loyalty, and open standards requirements. Here is what the law actually establishes.
articles.title: Utah SB 275 Explained: What the SEDI Law Actually Does
